evidence.title: Assisted mathematics performance and later unaided learning diverge in a bounded trial
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Bastani and colleagues report a classroom-randomized study of nearly 1,000 Turkish high-school students across four mathematics sessions. GPT Base and teacher-informed GPT Tutor increased assisted practice scores by 48% and 127% relative to control. Subsequent unassisted examination scores were 17% lower with Base; Tutor scores were statistically indistinguishable from control. Observation context: Fall semester of academic year 2023–2024.
evidence.evidence_standing: Author-reported bounded study; not independently reproduced by the Commons
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying comparison; founding definitions and classifications unchanged

source_locations.SRC-148: Experimental Design; Main Results, Table 1; Discussion

evidence.limitations: One school, grades 9–11, short exposure; assisted scores and immediate unassisted learning are different outcomes. Reduced acquisition does not establish erosion of established skills. Tutor required labor-intensive teacher inputs. Reported percentages are relative changes, not percentage points; no long-term outcome established. A statistically indistinguishable Tutor result does not establish equivalence or a positive unaided learning benefit.
evidence.open_questions: Which results transfer to other populations, tool versions, longer periods and operational governance settings? No such transfer is established by inclusion.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: The learning-acquisition boundary limits interpretation as established-skill decay. Better assisted practice need not imply better unassisted learning.

terms.name: Competency decay
terms.definition: A decline in the human or organizational expertise needed to perform, verify, contest, or recover work that is repeatedly delegated to AI-enabled systems. It is especially consequential when skills needed for independent judgment are lost.

terms.name: Outcome–purpose divergence
terms.definition: A condition in which meeting an immediate objective or metric degrades the benefit or purpose that justified pursuing it. The divergence can occur through narrow measures or indirect consequences without an intent to deceive.
